===Etymology 1===
From {{inh|en|enm|rung}}, from {{inh|en|ang|hrung}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*hrungu}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*hrungō}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|rong|t=pole, stanchion}}, {{cog|de|Runge|t=stake, pole, stanchion}}, {{cog|got|𐌷𐍂𐌿𐌲𐌲𐌰|t=a staff}}.

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}
[[File:Rungs of ladders and chair (PSF).png|thumb|Rungs of ladders and chair (PSF)]]

# A [[crosspiece]] forming a [[step]] of a [[ladder]]; a [[round]].
#: {{syn|en|spoke}}
# A [[crosspiece]] between [[leg]]s of a [[chair]].
# {{lb|en|figurative}} A [[position]] in a [[hierarchy]].
#: {{syn|en|echelon}}
#: {{ux|en|the lowest '''rung''' of the society}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2023-06-15|author=Kat Moon|title=Ashley Park’s Main Character Energy From ‘Joy Ride’ Is Here To Stay: ‘I’m Treating Myself Like A Lead Now’|journal={{w|Women's Health (magazine)|Women's Health}}|url=https://www.womenshealthmag.com/life/a44080288/ashley-park-joyride-interview/|passage=“I’m very proud that I’ve worked on every '''rung''' of the ladder,” Ashley says. “When you go to college, you don’t want to be a senior right away—you want to be a freshman.”|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260906190924/https://www.womenshealthmag.com/life/a44080288/ashley-park-joyride-interview/|archivedate=6 September 2026}}
# {{lb|en|nautical|dated}} A [[floor]] [[timber]] in a [[ship]].
# {{lb|en|dated}} One of the [[stake]]s of a [[cart]]; a [[spar]]; a heavy [[staff]].
# {{lb|en|engineering|dated}} One of the [[radial]] [[handle]]s [[project]]ing from the [[rim]] of a [[steering wheel]].
# {{lb|en|engineering|dated}} One of the [[pin]]s or [[trundle]]s of a [[lantern wheel]].

===Etymology 2===
{{nonlemma}}

====Verb====
{{head|en|verb form}}

# {{past participle of|en|ring|nocat=1}} {{qualifier|only in senses related to a bell}}
# {{lb|en|chiefly|_|dialectal}} {{infl of|en|ring||spast}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1723|author=Charles Walker|title=Memoirs of Sally Salisbury|section=VI
|passage=With ecchoing Shouts the vaulted Chamber '''rung''', / ''Belle Chuck'' was now the ''TOAST'' of ev'ry Tongue.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|journal=Report of State Officers, Board and Committees to the General ...|page=229|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=YHYbAQAAIAAJ|author=South Carolina. General Assembly|year=1906|passage=Mr. Seibels, in his testimony, said I '''rung''' him up to see about labels. He is very much mistaken. I '''rung''' him up to see about bottles.}}

====Adjective====
{{en-adj|-}}

# Of a pig: having a ring through the nose.
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=1842|journal=American Turf Register and Sporting Magazine|volume=13|page=335
|passage={{...}} he passed by his gate with a decided scowl on his furrowed brow, and grunting and growling like a newly '''rung''' pig.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=1919|journal=Popular Science|volume=95|issue=4|page=31
|passage=A "'''rung'''" pig is comfortable as long as he confines his food hunt to the surface of the ground. Ringing a pig of ordinary size is easy, but special arrangements must be made for handling the big ones.}}

====Usage notes====
{{m|en|rang|Rang}} and {{m|en|rung}} are incorrect for the past of {{m|en|ring}} in the sense of {{m|en|encircle}}, where {{m|en|ringed}} is used instead.

{{m|en|rung|Rung}} as a simple past is usually considered incorrect.
